image_description: The image displays a disassembled bassoon laid out on a stand against a white wall. The instrument is broken down into its primary sections: the boot (bottom U-shaped joint), two long wing joints, and the bell section at the top left. A black bocal case hangs on the wall above. The wood is a polished reddish-brown maple with silver-plated keywork. The components are arranged vertically, showcasing the length and complexity of the instrument.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although disassembled, the individual sections (wing joints) are visibly long, and their combined length implies a considerable total height consistent with a bassoon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The 'boot' joint at the bottom clearly exhibits the characteristic U-shape where the bore doubles back. The bell section is separate but identifiable as the flared end.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal bore structure is not visible from the exterior view; this feature cannot be visually verified without an X-ray or cutaway view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The actual metal bocal is not inserted into the instrument. A black case hanging on the wall likely contains it, but the component itself is not visible/attached to the instrument body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver-plated keys, rods, and pads are clearly visible running along the length of the wooden joints.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell section (top left) clearly flares outward. The 'held diagonally' part is context-dependent and not applicable to a static display, but the physical feature of the flared bell is present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wood exhibits a deep reddish-brown hue with a glossy, polished finish typical of maple bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The keywork reflects light with a silver/chrome appearance, consistent with silver-plating.
The main body components are clearly constructed from turned wooden tubes.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The bell section appears to float slightly disconnected or loosely attached to the upper wing joint. The mechanical linkage (tenon) seems vague or melted, lacking the precise tight fit expected in high-quality instrument photography.

artifact_observations.location: Keywork on the right-hand wing joint
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some of the smaller keys and rods appear slightly soft or fused into the wood body, lacking crisp edges. The reflection on the metal is somewhat inconsistent, suggesting minor generative blur.
The seat strap hook and the very bottom of the boot joint seem to merge slightly with the stand/wall shadow, creating a minor grounding ambiguity.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of woodwind instrument and distinguish it from similar instruments like the contrabassoon or oboe.
To verify the physical separation between the metal keys and the wooden body, ensuring no 'melting' or fusion artifacts exist in the complex keywork.
To analyze the spatial relationship between the disassembled parts and the stand, checking for floating elements or incorrect depth ordering.
To assess general sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any low-level noise or compression artifacts that might mimic AI generation errors.

focus_areas: Integrity of the keywork mechanism (are keys distinct from the wood?)
Connection points between the disassembled joints (do they look physically compatible?)
Realism of the wood grain and polish reflections
Grounding of the instrument on the stand
